## Detailed entries

### Adair County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-03-18, per signed Adair County Board of Supervisors minutes: Resolution #2026-26 adopted by unanimous 5-0 roll call (Hoadley, Baier, Wedemeyer, Christoffersen, Walker all aye).
- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-18` (exact)
- **Duration:** Not captured in news report; resolution text not yet obtained
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ia-adair-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution #2026-26, "Resolution to Establish a Temporary Moratorium on the Construction of Data Centers, High-Density Computing Facilities, and Battery Storage Facilities in the Unincorporated Areas of Adair County, Iowa," adopted March 18, 2026 by unanimous 5-0 roll call.
- **What prompted it:** Proposed 765 kV MISO transmission line, land negotiations in the Hebron area, and concern that data centers require large amounts of electricity and water.
- **Affected projects:** Applied Digital interest in a 200 MW data center near Adair reported in Clarke County coverage; no Adair County project approval record captured.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-07-31. Official minutes through 2026-07-15 show a draft data center ordinance was discussed (March 25, 2026 meeting: Supervisor Hoadley presented an AI-drafted ordinance for County Attorney review) but never formally adopted, so Resolution #2026-26's temporary moratorium remains in force.
- **Outcome:** Supervisors continued reviewing a draft data center ordinance after adoption of the moratorium. The draft would require data-center equipment to be housed in permanent structures on foundations, not shipping containers or similar temporary structures (March 25, 2026 Western Iowa Today: "No action was taken on the ordinance today" — confirms ordinance was still in draft a week after the moratorium passed).

### Jackson County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** Three documented adoptions in the captured record: (1) 2024-09-17 — Resolution #1066-09-17-2024 — "Resolution Approving Moratorium on Data Mining Facilities" (signed copy in record), originally through 2025-06-30 (text reads "for a period of months through June 30, 2025"). (2) 2025-09-09 — Resolution #1142-09-09-2025 — second moratorium re-established at the September 9, 2025 BoS meeting (signed minutes capture the motion and adoption). The interim 2025-03-25 "Resolution #1105-03-25-2025" referenced in earlier project notes is not corroborated in the captured Jackson County record and may have been a transcription of the 2024 resolution number; treat as ****.
- **Normalized date:** `2024-09-17` (exact)
- **Duration:** First instance (Sept 17, 2024) ran through June 30, 2025 (Resolution #1066-09-17-2024 text). Second instance (Sept 9, 2025) runs through August 31, 2026 unless ended sooner by board action (Resolution #1142-09-09-2025: "approving a Moratorium on Data Mining Facilities until August 31, 2026, unless ended sooner by action of the Board of Supervisors").
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `ia-jackson-county-2024`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution #1066-09-17-2024 (initial); Resolution #1142-09-09-2025 (re-establishment). Both adopted by Supervisors Schwenker, Steines, Flagel. The Citizen Portal article on the March 17, 2025 [sic — likely March 17, 2026] zoning commission meeting recounted that "a previous moratorium on data-mining facilities enacted in September 2024 [was] later rescinded; several members of the public said the moratorium's intent…had not been fully satisfied before the applicant filed." This reporting confirms the rescission/lapse between June 30, 2025 and the September 9, 2025 re-establishment.
- **What prompted it:** Resolution text cites lack of current county ordinance and need to protect infrastructure, natural resources, and property rights through adequate setback provisions while the Planning and Zoning Commission gathers information and coordinates with multiple agencies.
- **Affected projects:** One Aurum Capital Ventures bitcoin/data-mining special-exception application (project sized at about 2.5 megawatts) was the subject of a unanimous March 17, 2026 zoning commission recommendation against the applicant (recommend keep parcel A-1 zoning, deny special exception); applicant John Holberic represented Aurum Capital Ventures.
- **Detailed status:** Active. The March 25, 2025 moratorium (Resolution #1105-03-25-2025) was never rescinded -- it expired naturally on 2025-08-31 per its own terms, per the recitals of the resolution that replaced it. It was re-enacted via Resolution #1142-09-09-2025, effective through 2026-08-31 unless ended sooner by Board action. As of 2026-07-31, no rescission or replacement ordinance has been confirmed in primary records; Planning & Zoning reportedly planned to present a proposed 12-month extension to the Board on 2026-07-28, but the meeting's minutes were not yet posted at research time and the outcome could not be confirmed.
- **Outcome:** County reserved right to terminate early upon adoption of an ordinance ("BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Jackson County Board of Supervisors reserves the right to end the moratorium prior to the approved term…upon completion of a satisfactorily developed Data Mining Facilities Ordinance"). No final county ordinance had been adopted as of the captured March 17, 2026 zoning commission meeting.

### Union County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-03-18 -- Board of Supervisors voted unanimously (Hopkins, Friday; Brown absent) to move forward with setting up the moratorium. The formal instrument, Resolution #21 FYR 25/26 (Moratorium on Data Centers), was adopted at the March 25, 2026 regular session by roll call vote (Brown aye, Hopkins aye, Friday aye, motion carried).
- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-25` (exact)
- **Duration:** Up to one year from adoption of Resolution #21 FYR 25/26 (adopted 2026-03-25); the Board stated it "may or may not act on this matter, but at the minimum, we plan to revisit this issue in one year."
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ia-union-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution #21 FYR 25/26, "Moratorium on Data Centers," adopted March 25, 2026 by roll call vote (Brown aye, Hopkins aye, Friday aye).
- **What prompted it:** County discussion of data centers, local utility and infrastructure concerns, and desire for a research committee.
- **Affected projects:** Southwest Iowa REC-owned data center discussed in media coverage; per March 23, 2026 Creston News, REC's Phil Kinser said the project is "much smaller compared to the figures presented by the county during the last meeting"; no MW listed. The pending year-long moratorium is expected to allow the Southwest Iowa REC project to continue development.
- **Detailed status:** Active. Resolution #21 FYR 25/26 was adopted March 25, 2026, imposing a moratorium on construction of data centers and other high-density facilities "for a period of up to one Year." A review of Union County board minutes from March 25 through July 22, 2026 found no subsequent rescission, extension, or replacement.
- **Outcome:** County created a data center committee whose members include: Phil Kinser (Southwest Iowa REC); Dillon Daughenbaugh; Jessica Hagen (Union County Assessor); Roger Vicker (Protect Our Land's Future); Christian Boehmer (Union County Engineer); Jeff Rice (SIRWA — Southern Iowa Rural Water Association).
